BFCM 2026 · US · D-6 · live snapshot 2026-11-21

Holiday marketing teardown: ReelShort

ReelShort has no holiday campaign. Its growth runs on always-on app install ads that pay for themselves episode by episode, and this year its parent cut that spend by 42%. At D-6 there is not one live US ad.

● Too early to call · so far: failing

ReelShort does not publish a channel split, so there is no honest sales-by-channel table here. The parent reports the operator as a whole, and the latest quarter is a group figure.

Verdict: did ReelShort's strategy work

Too early to call for this season. Peak has not run. What can already be read is worse than a flat season: the brand stopped advertising in the US, its search demand halved year on year, and the parent's own reporting shows the growth engine stalling. Last year's holiday needed no campaign and produced 97% growth; this year's is starting from a smaller base with the budget withdrawn.

What worked

  • Price held: no discount, no bundle, still $200 a year.
  • Free reach: 35 organic creator posts, 8.45M views.
  • Creative discipline: four creatives carried every US ad in the library.

What didn't

  • No holiday campaign at all, in the one quarter that matters.
  • US ads stopped in July and never came back.
  • Brand search halved year on year before the peak even started.

Plays to copy

Sell the cliffhanger, not the app

Every top post is a title, one line of plot, and an unfinished sentence. The app is the punchline.

Watch: views per post

Seed codes, not ads

20 of 62 posts carry a creator code. That is distribution you can count.

Watch: signups per code

Keep one intro price running

The intro week is the promotion. It runs year round, so nothing has to be built in November.

Watch: conversion to paid

Post daily, cheaply

7 trailers a day at near-zero cost beats one campaign film.

Watch: cost per post

Do not discount the subscription

ReelShort held $19.99 to $21.99 through the season.

Watch: ARPU

Things to skip

  • Building a holiday landing page. ReelShort had none and the season still ran.
  • Cutting UA into the peak. The 42% cut lines up with the drop; that link is INFERRED, not proven.
  • Buying search on your own brand. ReelShort spent about $5 a month on it.
Method. SEEN means a call result or an image showed it; INFERRED means it was reasoned from what was seen. Counts are pulled where the source allows: 270 Meta ad instances, 62 creator posts, 523 owned posts, 15 weeks of activity per season. Money is an estimate with a range.

Pulled 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21. Meta Ad Library US, SpyFu US, DataForSEO US, App Store US, COL Group filings via secondary sources. Owned Instagram reaches back only to Oct 10 2026 and TikTok owned to Apr 29 2026. ReelShort's true user-acquisition budget is not public.

D-6: Black Friday Nov 27, peak ends Cyber Monday Nov 30.
